notes: OPEN [decision, Shafer, 2026-11-13]: esters are cleared in blood or gut, so cardiac output does not change their clearance (Shafer). Remimazolam is an ester, but its esterase is hepatic CES1 and severe hepatic impairment lowered its clearance 38% (Stohr 2021); the library model's clearance, 1.12 L/min, is 80% of the 1.4 L/min hepatic blood flow, which would make it flow-limited if hepatic. Whether to treat it as hepatic (cardiac output and liver function both act) or as an extrahepatic ester (neither acts) is not decided; until then it is pending and ignores the sliders.
